title: Red Happy's drum outfit and the bass drum cymbal beater
summary: Frazier describes Happy's drum set and how the bass drum's side cymbal mechanism worked and could be released for soft passages.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Early drum kits and the gear drummers used

blocks.x: He did some medium. I don't know about him singing in all this. He did lots of comedy work on the stage too, you see. I don't know if he ever, I never did see him play while the band, I mean sing while the band was playing. Most likely they'd be playing for the vaudeville show, you see. go there regular to watch the play? I used to sit right down in that time they called it the orchestra. Yeah, yeah. We used to call that, it was all colored show theater, you see, I used to sit right behind the band. What kind of a drum set did he have, drum outfit, you know, what kind? Oh, all I can remember was there was a yellow looking bass drum. I wouldn't know the name of it, you know what I mean? And four carbells, small side tum-tums, and the rattlers and the regular crash cymbals, and he was a very fast acted drummer. Two cymbals he had? I don't remember two cymbals. I know he had the old time crash cymbals with the side cymbals on the side of
the bass drum. How would those cymbals work on the bass drum? Well, they work, you see,

you had a beater, you had the overhead beaters on the bass drum, and you had like a hammer on the side of it. You could release it, you know, when you want to play the bass drum without hitting that side cymbal, you just could take your stick and raise that lever up, you see, it was working this motion like this, and you could take your sand and just raise it up, and you wouldn't hit the cymbal. But it hit exactly the same time? Same time with the beater, with your bass drum ball, yeah. They both hit the same time, and playing, if you want to release that, and your overheads used to fasten the top of your bass drum, and with a spring, make the spring actions, and you had to the flow, you used to have a pedal, a wooden pedal, and you fasten that again, the ball used to work over on this motion, like from overhead, and then you had a strap down, it used to meet the foot pedal, you see, and then they used to work it that way. Then you could have your cymbal always to your right of your bass, and you'd be sitting and you'd, similar like this, this mute on this bass drum now. And when you beat, otherwise the bass beat the ball in the, that hammer used to hit the cymbal at the same
time, same beat here. So, and then you'd let, you let it off for the softer passages, would
you, this thing? Yeah, yeah, you'd just release it for softer passages, that's right, yeah.
